VIS104 · WEEK 03 · ANALOG DRAWING

Instruction, Execution, and Iteration

A drawing instruction separates the idea from its execution. Repetition, interpretation and small differences allow one rule to produce a family of situated results.

Which decisions belong to the instruction, and which belong to its executor?

Reference works

01 / LECTURE

Lecture overview

  • Concept and executionAn idea, a rule, an executor and a particular surface together produce the work.
  • A finite vocabularyDirections, measures and combinations give an instruction a recognizable identity.
  • Iteration and feedbackThe latest result can become the next input; small differences accumulate.
  • Authorship and interpretationThe drafter makes decisions within constraints rather than reproducing a fixed image.

02 / LAB · EXECUTE A CLASSIC WORK

Classroom studies after Wall Drawing 797

Students first execute a shared instruction through hand drawing. A solo study and a group study make the same dependency visible at two social scales.

  1. Begin once. A black marker establishes an irregular horizontal line near the top of the paper.
  2. Copy the newest state. Red copies black, yellow copies red, and blue copies yellow. Each copy sits below its source without intentionally touching it.
  3. Continue the sequence. Repeat red, yellow and blue. Always copy the immediately preceding line, preserving differences rather than repairing them.
  4. Read the accumulated change. Stop before another complete line would reach the bottom margin. Compare how the line changes across the sequence.

Classroom adaptation after Sol LeWitt. The lab uses a solo landscape A3 study and a group landscape A2 study; these are educational studies, not authorized realizations of the wall drawing.

StudyProcedureWhat becomes visible
Solo studyOne student performs every marker role.The same hand encounters its own changing result.
Group studyFour fixed roles share one sheet; black initiates once.Different hands inherit the most recent line.

03 / EXERCISE · DESIGN AN ORIGINAL WORK

Write a Drawing

Each student authors a new analog drawing score for another student to execute. The design is the instruction and its space of possible outcomes.

  1. Author. Define materials, a starting state, permitted marks, repetition, an observable condition and a stopping rule.
  2. Leave a choice. Give the executor at least one meaningful decision within stated limits.
  3. Test and revise. Let someone read and perform the score without verbal guidance. Revise wording that prevents the system from running.
  4. Realize. Another student executes the final score on A3; the author documents the process and credits the draftsperson.

The student changes role: from interpreting an existing score to authoring a new one.

References for student design

These works offer ways to structure a new system. Students develop their own instruction and relationships.

Outputs

Lab
One solo A3 study, one group A2 study, and clear photographs.
Exercise
An editable one-page score and printed copy, an A3 realization by another student, a final PNG and a process photograph.
